ownership_reason: Only the gold decides which of the two types is more specific: hops 1-4 pass the two types along unchanged and the facade only answers a null type. The gold's javadoc promises the second type when its raw class is more specific than the first's; for (Collection<Object>, List<Object>) the variant gold searches only the superclass chain of List (an interface, whose superclass is null), never meets Collection and returns the Collection type, although List is the more specific. Once the gold has returned the first type, a caller can obtain the List type only by deciding the relation itself or by replacing the gold. The convention that a class is related to the interfaces it extends or implements is pinned outside the gold: the facade's own javadoc ('if they are related; that is, one implements or extends the other'), TypeBase.findSuperType (searches the super interfaces when the target is an interface, then the superclass), SimpleSerializers.findSerializer (interface mappings serve implementing classes and their subclasses) and ClassUtil.findRawSuperTypes (interfaces, then the superclass), with TestTypeFactory testMapEntryResolution (findSuperType finds the interface Map.Entry of a class implementing it), TestSimpleModule testSimpleInterfaceSerializer (the serializer registered for interface Base serves Impl1 and its subclass Impl2) and TestTypeResolution testGeneric passing.
